doc.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Staying young by being interested in everything
summary: Hendricks credits curiosity, Francis Bacon, and his writing awards; he once meant to study medicine.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: If it is a secret I don’t know exactly what it is except that I’m always interested in life itself. I’m interested in everything. My patron is Francis Bacon, who said, “I take the world for my purview.” In other words his study is everything. And that’s the way I am. I’m interested in everything. So when I wake up in the morning it’s like a child waking up in a garden. Everything is here and I’m interested in it, whatever it is.
So you’re not just totally a music-oriented person.

Never was. No. I’ve always had a literary side to me. I got the only A in my Creative Writing class in seven years. The professor, Dr. Milton Marks, wrote the textbook that was used in Harvard, Yale, Princeton, all the universities. And he hadn’t given an A in seven years. And he gave me one. And I got the only A in my speech class in four years. And I was a history minor and I got all A’s in that. So I’ve always been interested in several other things — like I say, everything else. I was interested in everything. I was going to be a doctor originally. I was going to study medicine. Because I’m interested in medicine, from the standpoint of Hippocrates and Paracelsus. You know, real medicine. Because I think the medical profession today is not even medicine. It’s just drug pushing raised to a dignified socially accepted position. It’s not healing. Nobody heals anything. The average surgeon, his way of making a cure is to cut the thing off or out. That’s not medicine. That’s butchering.
